questions.stem: A toxin makes the inner mitochondrial membrane permeable to protons. What happens to O₂ consumption and ATP synthesis?
questions.explanation: Uncoupling dissipates the gradient: electron flow (O₂ use) accelerates while ATP synthesis falls and heat rises. B: That pattern fits ETC or ATP synthase inhibitors. C: ATP can't rise without the gradient. D: Not possible. E: The gradient is lost.

questions.stem: Why do electrons from succinate yield fewer ATP (~1.5) than electrons from malate (~2.5)?

options.A: Succinate oxidation makes GTP instead of a reduced coenzyme
options.B: FAD(2H) passes them directly to cytochrome c
options.C: Complex II pumps protons back into the matrix
options.D: Malate dehydrogenase is coupled directly to ATP synthase
options.E: Succinate dehydrogenase passes them via FAD to CoQ, bypassing complex I

questions.explanation: Succinate dehydrogenase (complex II, the only TCA enzyme in the inner membrane) reduces FAD and passes electrons to CoQ, skipping complex I's proton pumping: 6 protons instead of 10. A: GTP comes from succinyl-CoA (succinate thiokinase). B: Electrons from complex II still pass through CoQ and complex III. C: Complex II doesn't pump protons at all. D: Malate's NADH enters at complex I; ATP synthase runs on the proton gradient.
questions.source: Energy Production, IX slides 16–18; VIII slides 29, 39

questions.stem: A child ingests a rodenticide and develops seizures and cardiac arrhythmias. Citrate accumulates in tissues. Which enzyme is inhibited?
questions.explanation: Fluoroacetate → fluorocitrate, which inhibits aconitase, so citrate accumulates. A: Citrate synthase forms fluorocitrate rather than being blocked. B: SDH inhibition would accumulate succinate. D: Cyanide/CO inhibit complex IV. E: Oligomycin inhibits ATP synthase.

questions.stem: Cytosolic NADH from glycolysis in skeletal muscle enters mitochondria via the glycerol 3-phosphate shuttle. Approximately how much ATP does each NADH yield?
questions.explanation: The G3P shuttle passes electrons to FAD → CoQ, bypassing complex I (6 protons → ~1.5 ATP). A: Too low. B: 2.5 is via the malate–aspartate shuttle. C: An older textbook value for matrix NADH. E: Too high.

questions.stem: A firefighter rescued from a burning building has headache, confusion, and severe lactic acidosis despite a normal PaO₂. Venous blood looks unusually bright red. Which ETC component is primarily inhibited?
questions.explanation: Cyanide (from burning plastics) and CO inhibit cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV), blocking O₂ use; tissues can't extract O₂ → bright venous blood and lactic acidosis. B: Rotenone inhibits complex I. C: Malonate-type inhibitors affect complex II. D: Antimycin A inhibits complex III. E: Oligomycin inhibits ATP synthase.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man with alcohol use disorder has confusion, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia. Which blood finding is expected from his vitamin deficiency?
questions.explanation: Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome: thiamine (TPP) deficiency impairs the α-keto acid dehydrogenases (PDH, α-KGDH, branched-chain), so pyruvate, α-ketoglutarate and other α-keto acids accumulate in blood. A: Citrate accumulates when aconitase is blocked (fluoroacetate). B: Methylmalonate rises in vitamin B12 deficiency. D: Succinate would rise with a block at succinate dehydrogenase. E: Pyruvate that can't enter PDH is shunted to lactate, so lactate rises.

questions.stem: α-Ketoglutarate is withdrawn from the TCA cycle for amino acid synthesis, and acetyl-CoA starts to accumulate. Which enzyme mainly restores the cycle?
questions.explanation: Removing any intermediate depletes oxaloacetate, so acetyl-CoA can't enter. Pyruvate carboxylase (biotin, ATP) makes oxaloacetate from pyruvate and is activated by acetyl-CoA, the signal that oxaloacetate is short. A: PDH supplies acetyl-CoA, not 4-carbon intermediates. B: Citrate synthase consumes oxaloacetate. C: PEPCK removes oxaloacetate for gluconeogenesis. D: α-KGDH consumes α-ketoglutarate.

questions.stem: Approximately how many ATP are produced when one acetyl-CoA is oxidized by the TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation?
questions.explanation: 3 NADH × 2.5 + 1 FAD(2H) × 1.5 + 1 GTP = 10. A: 12 uses older values (3 ATP per NADH, 2 per FAD(2H)). C: 7.5 counts only the NADH. D: 9 leaves out the GTP. E: 2.5 is the yield of one NADH.
